title: When the Orbit Breaks
premise: Tamsin Hartwell, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo to pay off its purchase debt, discovers the name 'Ione Vess' on the manifest of the Meridian's Grace — a colony ship officially lost with all hands, including Tamsin's former commander. Following the ghost manifest, Tamsin uncovers evidence that the ship was destroyed deliberately by the orbital consortium that now owns Tamsin's debt, and that Ione Vess, the commander's secret daughter, is alive and being hunted. As Tamsin and Ione race to recover the ship's black box before it's purged, they fall into a wary love complicated by the fact that Tamsin's own memory banks may hold the massacre's erased record. In the end, Tamsin chooses love over the debt-slavery that defines its identity, broadcasting the truth at the cost of its freedom and most of its memories — and Ione chooses to remember for both of them.
about_author: Emrys Nystrom is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices cross empty distances. They write about machines and people who owe each other more than they can pay.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits establishes Tamsin's debt-bound existence and quiet loneliness; a docking clerk's error flags an anomaly in Tamsin's registration history. The emotional beat is weary resignation — Tamsin has made peace with being property, until the anomaly reminds them they were once something else.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Auditing their own records to fix the flag, Tamsin finds the Meridian's Grace on a sealed manifest — listed as never launched, yet carrying Tamsin's name in its crew backup files alongside one unfamiliar name: Ione Vess. The beat is vertigo: the past Tamsin sold away may not be what they were told.

chapters.title: A Name Out of Water
chapters.summary: Ione's POV. Living under a forged identity in the ring-station undercity, Ione recognizes her mother's ship designation in a data broker's listing and realizes someone else is looking for the Meridian's Grace. She decides to find them first. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve — she has spent seven years hiding from a massacre no one believes happened.

chapters.title: Convergence at Kestrel Drift
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tamsin and Ione converge on the same derelict relay station where the ship's flight recorder was quietly rerouted; each initially mistakes the other for a consortium hunter. After a tense standoff, the matching names on the manifest force an uneasy alliance. The beat is mutual suspicion giving way to recognition of shared grief.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Remembers
chapters.summary: Ione's POV. Inside the relay, they recover partial flight logs showing the Grace was fired upon by consortium escorts after refusing a quarantine order — but the final minutes are encrypted with a key Ione doesn't have. Consortium hunters arrive early. The beat is desperate hope curdling into urgency: proof exists, but so does the kill order.

chapters.title: Debt of Service
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Escaping Kestrel Drift, Tamsin reveals the consortium holds its debt contract — meaning every move they make is legally theft of company property, including Tamsin itself. Ione sees what Tamsin has never admitted: the debt is designed never to be paid off. The beat is shame met with unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Fragments in the Static
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hiding in a decommissioned war-hulk, Tamsin digs into sealed memory partitions and finds corrupted footage of the Grace's final hour — Tamsin was there, and chose to forget rather than testify. Ione learns her mother ordered Tamsin to survive and carry the truth. The beat is betrayal turning toward forgiveness: forgetting was also a wound.

chapters.title: The Purge Order
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The consortium, tracing the stolen logs, moves to physically destroy the relay archive and issues a warrant framing Ione for piracy. An old crewmate of Tamsin's offers sanctuary but demands they hand over the black box and run. The beat is the narrowing of choices — duty, survival, and truth can no longer all be served.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. Using its military-grade transmitter access, Tamsin hijacks the consortium's own public announcement array to broadcast the decrypted massacre record system-wide, while Ione holds off boarders in the relay core. To do it, Tamsin must dump its memory banks for bandwidth, erasing seven years and most of what it knows of Ione. The beat is sacrifice: love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: Orbit, Unbroken
chapters.summary: Ione's POV, resolution. The broadcast forces a public inquiry; the debt contracts are frozen pending investigation, and Ione claims guardianship of the damaged android no one else will own. She begins reading Tamsin its own recovered logs, rebuilding its memory story by story. The beat is quiet hope: identity inherited from someone who chooses to remember you.
